277: Another explanation: How good and how pleasant it is, etc. — these are those friends, when they come to dwell together, they do not separate from one another. At first, they appear like men preparing for war, who want to kill one another. Afterwards they return to love and brotherhood. What does the Holy One, blessed be He, say? How good and how pleasant it is when brothers also dwell together. "Also," is to include the divine presence with them. And not only that, the Holy One, blessed be He, listens to their words, and it is pleasant for Him and He rejoices in them. That is that which is written: Then they who feared the Lord spoke to one another: and the Lord hearkened, and heard it, and a book of remembrance was written before Him, etc. (Malachi 3:16).

And you, friends here, just like you have been with harmony and love before now, so too should you not separate one from the other from now on, until the Holy One, blessed be He, connects with you and calls out peace upon you. So peace will be found in the world for your sake. That is [the meaning of] that which is written: For the sake of my brothers and friends, I pray peace be with you (Psalms 122:8).
